item.title: Windy night at the end of Mount Batten Breakwater
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was a great night. According to the forecast, we had winds of 37kmh gusting 51.8kmh at 8pm (we were off the water at eight). I make that 22mph with gusts of 32mph which puts us in Beaufort 5 territory.

item.title: Drakes Island - outside Breakwater
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: It was nice to get back in the Sea Kayak. I make the distance paddled around 8.5 miles (using a string and map). Although the wind patterns were interesting (there was a bit of wind in the morning, I think it might have moved and we were sheltered in the afternoon) it was enough to make balance “interesting” in places. I can’t remember the forecast probabilities of rain, and whilst it spotted we never did see any. There was negligible swell, just enough to keep the rock hopping interesting. Low tide was 12:50; I figure we were on the breakwater between 11 and 12.

item.title: First training session of the season
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: So this was shortly after the watch change and the first opportunity to get on the water one afternoon for a couple of hours in Plymouth. For no particular reason I used a club boat (a short cove boat, similar to my B2 which turns 180 degrees with only one edge). I did, however, take my shiny (for me) new Werner Shuna paddle (set to 45% and 115cm).

item.title: Short windy trip to Cable Beach
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: So I’ve had a few problems with Asthma (cold weather and viruses) as well as being on a First Aid course for two weeks. Therefore, I opted to do the short paddle on the 22nd. Firstly, I forgot to recharge my camera, so the only photo I have is from the other group (that did the so-called long paddle). However, it turns out they did almost the same paddle as us (maybe a mile more). This photo captures some sense of the swell on the day.

item.title: Drakes Island and beyond Penlee Point
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description:
Photo Credit: Terry Calcott

This was a cold paddle, with a little bit of wind coming from the North. We started off as a single group with two paddlers on their first Saturday paddle. At Fort Picklecombe, the leader decided to split us into two groups; one going to Mount Edgcumbe for lunch and the other to Cawsand. As it turned out, we went a little beyond Penlee point and had lunch at a beach (Sandway’s beach?) before returning home.

item.title: Penlee Point and Cawsand
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description:
Photo Credit: Paul Hewson

This was an interesting day, sandwiched between outburts of Storm Éowyn saw very little wind, but some large low frequency swell. My weather API suggested 2m; it was hard to believe it was that big. However, it was low frequency, and I didn’t get far enough away from anyone to “calibrate” my call on this. Indeed, we managed to paddle across the sound outside the breakwater.

item.title: Mountbatten to Wembury
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description:
Photo Credit: Helga Pinn Facebook

This was a cold, dark and very flat day. Nice paddle though. Over 12 miles. Did some rock hopping in unchallenging conditions.
